keys.title: API keys
keys.subtitle: Keys let another system (accounting, ERP, a marketplace, a dashboard) read your shop's data without a staff login. Keys can only read, never change anything.
keys.readOnly: You can see the keys but not change them.
keys.searchPlaceholder: Search by name or key start

keys.emptyDescription: Create a key when another system needs to read your orders, products or stock.
keys.rotateDescription: A new key is created and shown once. The old key stops working at once, so any system still using it will be refused until you give it the new key.
keys.deleteDescription: The key stops working at once and cannot be brought back. Create a new key if you need one later.

keyForm.newDescription: Choose what the key may read. The key itself is shown once, after you save.
keyForm.editDescription: The key itself does not change. To get a new key value, use Rotate.

keyForm.nameHint: Who or what uses this key, for example Accounting sync.
keyForm.scopesHint: Choose only what the other system really needs.

keyForm.branchHint: Orders and stock of other branches stay hidden from this key.

errors.noScope: Choose at least one access right.

errors.expiryPast: The expiry must be in the future.

usage.title: How to use a key
usage.intro: Send the key in the X-Api-Key header of every request. Never put it in the web address. In the example, YOUR_API_KEY stands for the key you copied when you created it.
usage.hostNote: Replace {host} with the address of your Juvo BD server (the API host). This staff site does not forward these requests; your technical contact can tell you the address.
usage.limits: Lists answer 20 items per page by default (up to 100). A key that sends too many requests in a minute gets a 429 answer with a Retry-After header.

hooks.title: Webhooks
hooks.subtitle: A webhook makes Juvo BD send a signed message to your system when something happens, for example when an order is placed. Addresses must be https and public.
hooks.readOnly: You can see the webhooks and their deliveries but not change them.
hooks.limitReached: The limit of {max} webhooks is reached. Delete one before adding another.
hooks.rotateLabel: Create a new signing secret for {name}
hooks.disabledToast: Webhook {name} is off. No new events are sent to it.
hooks.deletedToast: Webhook {name} and its delivery log were deleted.
hooks.emptyDescription: Add a webhook when another system should be told about orders, products or stock as they change.
hooks.rotateTitle: Create a new signing secret for {name}?
hooks.rotateDescription: A new secret is created and shown once. Requests are signed with it from now on, so your receiving system must be updated with the new secret.
hooks.deleteDescription: No more events are sent to this address and its delivery log is deleted. This cannot be undone.

hookForm.newDescription: Choose the address and the events. The signing secret is shown once, after you save.
hookForm.editDescription: The signing secret does not change. To get a new one, use New secret.
hookForm.name: Name
hookForm.nameHint: For your own reference, for example ERP orders.
hookForm.urlHint: Must start with https:// and point to a public server. No user name or password in the address. Addresses on private networks are refused.
hookForm.eventsHint: You can choose several. The test event is always available.

errors.unknownEvent: One of the chosen events is not known. Reload the page.

verify.title: Check that a request is from Juvo BD
verify.intro: Every request carries a Juvo-Signature header like t=1700000000,v1=abcdef... Your system should check it before it trusts the message.
verify.step1: Read t (seconds since 1970) and v1 from the header.
verify.step2: Compute the HMAC-SHA256 of the text t, a dot, and the raw request body, using the signing secret, as lower-case hex.
verify.step3: Compare it with v1 in constant time, and refuse the request if t is more than {seconds} seconds from your clock.
verify.step4: Each event has an id that is the same on every retry: ignore an id you have already handled.
verify.answer: Answer with any 2xx status within 5 seconds. A failed attempt is retried after 30 seconds, 2, 8 and 32 minutes; after the fifth failure it is marked failed and can be sent again from the log below.

log.title: Delivery log
log.intro: Every message sent to a webhook, newest first. Errors are short and never contain your address or the receiver's answer.
log.searchPlaceholder: Search by event or delivery id
log.selectFailed: Select the {count, plural, one {# failed delivery} other {# failed deliveries}} on this page
log.selected: {count, plural, one {# delivery selected} other {# deliveries selected}}
log.redeliverQueued: {count, plural, one {# delivery was queued again.} other {# deliveries were queued again.}}
log.redeliverRefused: {count, plural, one {# delivery was refused by the server.} other {# deliveries were refused by the server.}}
log.emptyDescription: Deliveries appear here after an event happens or after you send a test event.
log.confirmOne: The same message (same event id and body) is queued to be sent again with a fresh set of attempts. Your system should ignore it if it already handled this event id.
log.confirmBulkTitle: Send {count, plural, one {# delivery} other {# deliveries}} again?
log.confirmBulk: The same messages (same event ids and bodies) are queued again, each with a fresh set of attempts. Your system should ignore event ids it already handled.
